To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the place of articulation of Kannada coronals is more forward for nasals than for stops and laterals, and that the front of the tongue is more raised in nasals and laterally compared to stops.

1) the place contrast is greater for dental stops than for dental nasals and laterally; 2) the place contrast for retroflexes is greater for stops than for laterals and nasals; 3) the tongue body is more forward for nasal and lateral than for stop coronals, and 4) the tongue root is more retracted for retroflexes than for dentals, but the tongue root retraction is greater for stops and laterals than for nasals.

The tongue root and body positions of the tongue for the retroflex consonants of Kannada were more posterior compared to the dental consonants, but the front part of the dorsum was more forward for nasals and lateral compared to the dental stops.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
manner of articulation affects the place contrast in Kannada coronals, and the manner contrast in the coronal place of articulation is not a binary one.
the articulation of manner of articulation in a language is a dynamic process, and the acoustic correlates are a reflection of the articulatory gestures involved in producing the manner contrast.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the articulation of manner of articulation can be a factor in determining the place of articulation of coronal consonants, which is a factor not often considered in phonetic and phonological studies.
the place and manner of articulation are not independent, and that articulatory differences in place and manner can be observed even in languages that are typologically similar.
